findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`. It does not implement the abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` or the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` points to this class. For any detector of type `metric_alert_fire`, `Detector.detector_handler` will call `group_type.detector_handler(self)` and raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`, which crashes `process_detectors`. Before this change the handler was concrete and returned an empty result. Either keep a concrete stub implementing the abstract methods, or don't wire the handler until it is implemented.

findings.title: Expected occurrence built for wrong group key in test_dedupe
findings.body: `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` builds the expected occurrence with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)`. It then evaluates group key `"group_key"`. The fingerprint of the expected occurrence (`<id>:val1`) therefore differs from the actual result (`<id>:group_key`). With dataclass equality on `IssueOccurrence`, the equality assertion should fail. If it passes, the test is not checking what it claims. Build the expected occurrence with the same group key that is evaluated.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` now returns a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". This misleads implementers about the new return contract.
